subject: geography
title: The United Kingdom
description: The countries, capital cities and surrounding seas of the United Kingdom, and its human and physical features such as rivers, mountains and cities.

objectives.statement: Name and locate the four countries of the United Kingdom and their capital cities.
Name and locate the seas surrounding the United Kingdom.
Identify key physical features of the UK, such as mountains, rivers and coasts.
Identify key human features of the UK, such as cities, capitals and landmarks.

items.prompt: Name the four countries that make up the United Kingdom.
items.answer: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland

items.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of the four countries of the UK?

items.statement: Scotland is one of the four countries of the United Kingdom.

items.prompt: Which country is the largest of the four UK countries?

items.statement: 'Great Britain' means the same thing as 'the United Kingdom'.

items.prompt: What is the capital city of England?
What is the capital city of Scotland?
What is the capital city of Wales?
Belfast is the capital city of which country?

items.statement: London is the capital city of the United Kingdom.

items.prompt: The UK is surrounded by water. What do we call a large area of salt water like the one between the UK and France?
Which sea lies between the east coast of England and mainland Europe?

items.statement: The United Kingdom is an island nation surrounded by sea.

items.prompt: What do we call the place where the land meets the sea?

items.statement: The Irish Sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland.

items.prompt: What is the name for a large natural stream of water that flows into the sea, like the Thames or the Severn?
Which of these is the longest river in the United Kingdom?
Ben Nevis, the highest mountain in the UK, is found in which country?

items.statement: A mountain is a physical feature, made by nature rather than by people.
A city is a human feature because it is built by people.
